extraction.teacher_style: Michael Moloi guides students through traditional gumboot dance with energetic encouragement and structured breakdown of steps. He demonstrates each movement clearly from both front and back views while building up tempo progressively.

lesson_structure.note: Michael introduces himself and the history of gumboot dance.
Warm up coordination exercise combining hand claps and rhythm.
Explains body posture, protecting knees and back, and knee height.
Breaks down step number 1 slowly with hand and foot coordination.
Breaks down step number 3 (and cross and cross).
Practices steps 1, 2, and 3 together slowly from the back.
Practices steps 1, 2, 3, 4, and 5 together slowly from the back.

cues: and out and out and in and in
metaphors: protecting your knees and your back so you're in a spring
safety: Your body position needs to be here protecting your knees and your back so you're in a spring.

steps_taught.name: Step 1
steps_taught.description: Stepping out and hitting boots with hands in sequence.

steps_taught.name: Step 2
steps_taught.description: Double hits on right and left.

steps_taught.name: Step 3
steps_taught.description: Cross body hitting of the boots.

steps_taught.name: Step 4
steps_taught.description: Traveling side step pattern hitting boots.

steps_taught.name: Step 5
steps_taught.description: Slapping boots across the body alternating sides.

what_works: Clear progressive tempo buildup from slow to fast
Showing both front and back views for learning
what_hinders: No mirrors or multiple students to follow along with

quotes.text: Before we start gumboot, ladies and gentlemen, I want us to warm up a bit.
First, your body position needs to be here, protecting your knees and your back.
Facing this way, a little bit faster.
